treatment_plan.summary: 67-year-old female with non-valvular atrial fibrillation (CHA₂DS₂-VASc = 4) on warfarin (INR 2.4), who has undergone primary PCI with a drug-eluting stent for NSTEMI. She also has Type 2 Diabetes Mellitus. This complex scenario requires a tailored antithrombotic strategy balancing stroke prevention, stent thrombosis risk, and bleeding risk from triple therapy.

recommendations.intervention: Warfarin — maintain dose-adjusted to achieve an INR range of 2.0–2.5 while on triple or dual antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: Patient has high-risk non-valvular AF (CHA₂DS₂-VASc 4) requiring long-term OAC; INR target lowered to 2.0–2.5 when combined with antiplatelet agents to reduce bleeding risk.

recommendations.intervention: Aspirin 75-100mg/day orally — as part of initial triple antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: Following ACS with PCI in AF patient, triple therapy (VKA, aspirin, clopidogrel) should be considered in the short term (3–6 months).

recommendations.intervention: Clopidogrel 75 mg daily orally — as part of initial triple antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: Following ACS with PCI in AF patient, triple therapy (VKA, aspirin, clopidogrel) should be considered in the short term (3–6 months).

recommendations.intervention: Dabigatran etexilate 110 mg twice daily orally — as an alternative to VKA if patient is at higher risk of bleeding or unwilling to continue VKA monitoring
recommendations.rationale: Patient is elderly (67F) and will be on combination antithrombotic therapy, placing her at higher risk of bleeding; dabigatran 110 mg BD is an option for patients at higher bleeding risk (HAS-BLED ≥3).

recommendations.intervention: Dabigatran etexilate 150 mg twice daily orally — as an alternative to VKA if patient has low bleeding risk and prefers not to have regular INR monitoring
recommendations.rationale: For patients with non-valvular AF who are unwilling to go on VKA because of the inconvenience, dabigatran 150 mg twice daily may be considered, unless contraindicated.

recommendations.intervention: Rivaroxaban 15 mg daily orally + clopidogrel 75 mg daily — as an alternative to standard triple therapy to reduce bleeding risk (NOAC-based dual therapy)
recommendations.rationale: In patients with AF who have undergone PCI with drug-eluting stents, the use of NOAC with antiplatelet therapy is associated with a lower risk of bleeding than standard triple therapy (DAPT + warfarin).
contraindications_checked: Renal function (dose adjustment noted if eGFR 30-50 ml/min)

recommendations.intervention: Gastric protection with a proton pump inhibitor (PPI) — to be considered where necessary given triple or dual antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: CPG states gastric protection with a PPI should be considered where necessary for patients on antithrombotic combination therapy.

recommendations.intervention: ECG — baseline and ongoing monitoring for arrhythmias and ischaemic changes
recommendations.rationale: Baseline ECG required for all patients with AF and post-PCI monitoring.

recommendations.intervention: INR monitoring — weekly until stable, then at least monthly while on VKA-based triple therapy
recommendations.rationale: Patient is on warfarin and requires INR monitoring to ensure therapeutic range of 2.0–2.5 while on triple therapy.

recommendations.intervention: HAS-BLED bleeding risk assessment — to guide intensity and duration of antithrombotic therapy
recommendations.rationale: Assessment of the risk of bleeding should be considered when prescribing antithrombotic therapy; HAS-BLED score ≥3 indicates 'high risk' requiring caution and regular review.

recommendations.intervention: Creatinine clearance calculation (Cockcroft-Gault formula) — to guide drug dosing, especially for antithrombotic agents
recommendations.rationale: Drug doses should be adjusted according to renal function; this 67-year-old patient with diabetes may have impaired renal function.

recommendations.intervention: Statin therapy — for all patients with established CVD and diabetes aged >40 years, regardless of baseline LDL cholesterol level
recommendations.rationale: 67F with established CVD (post-NSTEMI, PCI) and T2DM meets criteria for statin therapy regardless of lipid levels.

monitoring.schedule: Weekly until stable on triple/dual therapy, then at least monthly
monitoring.target: INR 2.0–2.5 while on combination antithrombotic therapy

monitoring.schedule: At baseline and regularly while on antithrombotic therapy
monitoring.target: Score ≥3 indicates high risk requiring caution and regular review

monitoring.schedule: At baseline and as clinically indicated
monitoring.target: Drug dose adjustment per renal function

monitoring.parameter: Signs of bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, haematuria, bruising, intracranial haemorrhage symptoms)
monitoring.schedule: Ongoing clinical assessment at each visit
monitoring.target: Immediate review if significant bleeding occurs
Less than 8 mmol/L in the acute setting; optimal control following discharge

red_flags: Signs of major bleeding (haematemesis, melaena, intracranial haemorrhage symptoms, haemodynamic instability) — immediate medical review and consideration of anticoagulation reversal
INR >3.5 — increased risk of intracranial bleeding exponentially; hold warfarin and seek urgent review
Stent thrombosis symptoms (recurrent chest pain, ST changes, haemodynamic instability) — urgent assessment for re-PCI
Severe hypoglycaemia requiring third-party assistance — reassess antidiabetic medications and glycaemic targets, screen for CVD
follow_up: 1 month: Reassess bleeding events, review INR stability on triple therapy, assess tolerance of antithrombotic regimen — if stable, continue triple therapy for up to 3-6 months (ACS with DES)

3-6 months: Transition from triple therapy (VKA + aspirin + clopidogrel) to dual therapy (VKA + clopidogrel 75 mg daily, or alternatively aspirin 75-100 mg daily) — assess bleeding risk vs stent thrombosis risk
Up to 12 months: Continue VKA plus single antiplatelet (clopidogrel 75 mg daily preferred) — reassess for transition to VKA monotherapy
After 12 months: If stable vascular disease (>1 year, no acute events), consider VKA monotherapy alone without concomitant antiplatelet therapy per CPG guidance
Ongoing: Regular INR monitoring (target 2.0-2.5 on combination therapy, 2.0-3.0 as lifelong monotherapy), blood glucose monitoring, lipid profile review
unresolved_questions: The primary ICD code predicted (BA41.0 = STEMI) does not match the clinical presentation of NSTEMI — the alternate code 8B26.4 (non-ST elevation MI) is more appropriate and should be confirmed by the clinician.

The retrieved evidence predates the NOAC era for AF-PCI (e.g., PIONEER AF-PCI, RE-DUAL PCI, AUGUSTUS trials). The NOAC-based regimens cited from the CVD Risk CPG (chunk 2) are based on more recent evidence (rivaroxaban 15 mg daily + clopidogrel). Current best practice may favour apixaban-based regimens which are not fully detailed in the retrieved evidence.

Specific stent type (sirolimus-eluting vs paclitaxel-eluting) affects duration of triple therapy — CPG recommends at least 3 months for sirolimus-eluting and at least 6 months for paclitaxel-eluting stents. This needs to be confirmed.

Prasugrel is recommended for diabetics with ACS (chunk 6), but the AF CPG only mentions clopidogrel for triple therapy. Prasugrel use in triple therapy with VKA is not addressed in the retrieved evidence and carries higher bleeding risk.

Ticagrelor as an alternative P2Y12 inhibitor for ACS in AF patients on anticoagulation is not well addressed in the retrieved AF-PCI sections — the CVD Risk CPG (chunk 2) mentions ticagrelor 90 mg BD for ACS DAPT but not specifically in the AF-PCI context.

Glycaemic management for this patient with T2DM and ACS — the evidence recommends keeping blood sugars <8 mmol/L in the acute setting (chunk 6). Specific pharmacotherapy for diabetes in the post-ACS setting (e.g., SGLT2i, GLP-1RA with CV benefit) is addressed in the CVD Risk CPG (chunk 2, Figure 2) but not fully retrieved.

The CPG AF sections are from Malaysian CPGs that may be over 10 years old given the evidence base (RE-LY trial references). Newer international guidelines (ESC 2020, AHA/ACC) may have updated recommendations for AF-PCI antithrombotic strategies.

Expected referral not surfaced in plan: Cardiology — Atrial Fibrillation, urgency: routine (trigger: need further investigation/echocardiography). Evidence: Outpatient specialist referral is recommended for those who: Need further investigation/echocardiography No referral recommendation was emitted — clinician should arrange specialist input.
